result.summary:
Ran docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md item by item against the actual diff at commit d89e6c5 (branch feature/WF02-REQ-031). Read in full: apps/bot/src/domain/feedback.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/feedback.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts, apps/bot/drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql, plus the diffs for domain/registration.ts, domain/user.ts, domain/notification.ts, db/schema.ts against the pre-implementation commit. Did not trust REVIEWER's or BACKEND-DEV's characterizations -- re-derived each finding from the code and constructed the negative case for each applicable invariant.

S1 (consent precedes storage) -- PASS, independently scrutinized beyond the design doc's own claim. The design's framing ('every feedback respondent already holds an admitted+checked-in registration, so S1 is already satisfied before this flow starts') is correct for the STORE-MY-DATA consent, confirmed by tracing selectRegistrationsForFeedbackRequest/Reminder's isNotNull(checkedInAt) gate and getRegistrationFeedbackContext's re-check at compose time -- nobody without an existing consented User/Registration row can ever reach this flow. I separately asked whether storing free-text content (liked/improve/topicVotes) as a NEW category needs its own consent distinct from consent_pd_at: it does not, under S1's own table -- S1 names exactly three consent categories (store/message/publish), and free-text feedback content is not a fourth category the invariants file or PRD ยง10/ยง12 requires a separate consent for; it is authored voluntarily by an already-consented person in direct response to the bot's own prompt, the same treatment this codebase already gives profiles.public_bio (an existing free-text column stored under the same blanket consent_pd_at, no separate consent flow). No Feedback row can be created without nps (schema NOT NULL + writeFeedbackNps as sole INSERT path), and no optional field can be written before that row exists (UPDATE-only, gated by determineNextFeedbackField's ordering) -- so nothing about a new person is ever stored ahead of consent. PASS.

S2/S3 (ownership, no cross-user PII leak) -- PASS, this is the most security-critical question and was independently re-derived, not trusted. Traced parseFeedbackReplyContext (domain/feedback.ts) and all three write-adjacent call sites in handlers/feedback.ts:
  - makeFeedbackNpsCallbackHandler (lines 105-164): resolves flowUser from the TAPPING Telegram user's own tg_id via getFlowUserByTgId (never trusts anything in callback_data as an identity claim), then reads context = getRegistrationFeedbackContext(db, registrationId) from the callback_data-encoded registrationId, and explicitly checks `context.userId !== flowUser.id` (line 144) -- refusing with notYourFeedback and NO WRITE if the registration's actual owner differs from the tapping user. This is a real ownership check comparing the DB-resolved owner against the DB-resolved tapper, not merely confirming the registration exists.
  - makeFeedbackBroadcastCallbackHandler (lines 172-220): identical ownership check at line 200, same shape.
  - makeFeedbackTextReplyHandler (lines 227-282): parses registrationId AND field from the replied-to message text (never from the current message's own claims), resolves flowUser from tg_id, then at line 254 checks `context === null || context.userId !== flowUser.id` -- silently no-ops (correct for a passive listener) rather than alerting, but the ownership check is present and gates the write identically.
Constructed the negative case directly: if a registration belonging to User A were forwarded/leaked (e.g. A forwards their own NPS force_reply message, or a leaked callback_data string, to User B, and B taps/replies), flowUser resolves to B's own row via B's tg_id, context.userId resolves to A's id from the registration itself, the inequality check fires, and no write function is ever called for any of the three handlers -- confirmed by reading that in all three cases the write call (writeFeedbackNps / writeBroadcastOptInAnswer / writeFeedbackOptionalField|markFeedbackFieldSkipped) sits strictly after the ownership check and inside code paths the check would have already returned out of. B's own feedback state is also never touched (B's identity plays no role in the write; the write always targets A's own registrationId/A's own userId, which is exactly why B can never read or corrupt B's UNRELATED feedback via this route -- the leaked-token path can at most be a no-op against A's row, never a cross-contamination into B's row). No cross-user PII (A's liked/improve/topicVotes answers) is ever surfaced back to B either -- advanceFeedbackFlow only ever sends the NEXT PROMPT text (catalog copy), never echoes back a stored answer to anyone. PASS on both S2 and S3.

S9 (idempotency, no in-memory state) -- PASS. Both makeFeedbackRequestJob and makeFeedbackReminderJob (scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts) route every send through the existing sendLedgeredNotification (domain/notification.ts, REQ-025, reused unchanged) with distinct NotificationKinds ('feedback_request' vs 'feedback_reminder', confirmed as the only addition to the NotificationKind union). Idempotency is enforced by notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) DB constraint (REQ-025-schema.md, unchanged by this diff) -- not an in-memory set -- so a scheduler restart mid-batch re-runs the same selection query, re-attempts the same ledger insert, and collides on the already-written row, producing skipped-already-sent rather than a duplicate send. Constructed the negative case: killed/restarted mid-batch is exactly the case a DB-backed UNIQUE constraint (survives a process restart) is designed to cover, unlike an in-memory Set which would not. PASS.

S10 (transactional/marketing classification, blocked-user skip) -- PASS. Both jobs call sendLedgeredNotification with classification: 'transactional' explicitly (feedbackJobs.ts lines 179, 209). Read domain/notification.ts directly: step 2 (blocked check, line ~110-113) runs unconditionally BEFORE the classification branch -- 'if (user.blocked) return { kind: "skipped-blocked" }' -- for every send regardless of classification, so this new call site cannot bypass it; it uses the exact same sendLedgeredNotification entry point every other notification kind uses, no parallel/bypassing send path was introduced. AC7 (transactional sends ignore broadcast_opt_in) is satisfied because the classification branch that reads broadcastOptIn is structurally unreached for a 'transactional' kind (confirmed by reading the branch: broadcastOptIn is read only inside the marketing-classification branch). A blocked Telegram user therefore fails gracefully via the existing skipped-blocked outcome, not a crash -- no new exception path was added around this call site. PASS.

S11 (no PII in logs) -- PASS. Grepped apps/bot/src for console./logger./log( across all new/changed files (domain/feedback.ts, handlers/feedback.ts, scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts): zero matches. No feedback content (nps/liked/improve/topicVotes) or free-text answers are ever logged, and advanceFeedbackFlow only ever sends catalog-defined prompt copy back to the respondent themselves, never their own prior answer or another user's. No AuditLog write exists anywhere in this diff (grepped for auditLog/AuditLog across the new files: no matches in feedback.ts, handlers/feedback.ts, or feedbackJobs.ts) -- correctly so, since S8 only requires an AuditLog row for a status change, and feedback answers are not a Registration/EventStaff/admission status change; no PII is therefore at risk of leaking through an AuditLog payload either, since none is written. PASS.

S13 (migration safety) -- SIGNED OFF. Read apps/bot/drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql directly, not a description of it: CREATE TABLE feedback (new table, no existing data affected), ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN broadcast_opt_in_asked_at (nullable, no default, so every existing users row reads back NULL post-migration -- exactly the correct 'never asked' state, no backfill needed and no existing column value is altered), plus the FK (ON DELETE restrict, consistent with this schema's universal convention) and the UNIQUE index. No DROP, no RENAME, no column type change, no rewrite of any existing personal-data or attendance-history column. This migration does not fall under the 'drops, renames, or rewrites a column or table holding personal data or attendance history' trigger in this role's mandate, so no aggregate-preserving-anonymization concern applies -- confirmed by reading the SQL itself rather than trusting REQ-031-schema.md ยง6's own prose description of it, and the two matched byte-for-byte on every statement. Explicit sign-off: this migration is SAFE to run against a live production DB with existing rows.

Broadcast-opt-in / consent-boundary separation -- PASS. Read writeBroadcastOptInAnswer (domain/user.ts lines 281-291) in full: its only .set({...}) call touches broadcastOptIn and broadcastOptInAskedAt -- no reference to consentPdAt, consentPdVersion, or publishConsent anywhere in this function or anywhere else in the diff. Grepped domain/user.ts for consentPd/publishConsent usage: all occurrences are in pre-existing, untouched functions (resolveOrCreateUser, getFlowUserByTgId, createWalkinUser) that this diff does not modify. The three consent categories remain genuinely distinct records, never conflated. PASS.

Other invariants (S4-S8, S12, S14): N/A to this diff, with reason -- no qr_token/InviteCode generation or validation, no check-in logic, no capacity/admission-state changes, no CSV export, and no Profile/speaker publication touched anywhere in the changed files (domain/feedback.ts, handlers/feedback.ts, scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts, registration.ts's one new read-only function, user.ts's two new functions, notification.ts's one-line union addition, and the additive migration). Confirmed by reading the full diff stat and each changed file rather than assuming from the requirement's description.

invariant_verdicts.S1: PASS -- consent already satisfied before this flow starts (checked-in gate traced); free-text feedback content is not a 4th consent category under S1's own table
invariant_verdicts.S2: PASS -- ownership derived via getFlowUserByTgId(tg_id) vs registration.userId, never trusts callback_data/message text as an identity claim
invariant_verdicts.S3: PASS -- negative case constructed: a leaked/forwarded token from user A tapped/replied by user B refuses with no write in all three handlers (NPS callback, broadcast callback, text-reply listener); B's own feedback state cannot be corrupted via this route either
invariant_verdicts.S6: N/A -- no admission/checked_in_at logic touched (checkedInAt is read-only here)
invariant_verdicts.S8: N/A -- feedback answers are not a status change; correctly no AuditLog write added
invariant_verdicts.S9: PASS -- idempotency via notification_ledger UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), a DB constraint that survives process restarts, distinct kinds for request vs reminder
invariant_verdicts.S10: PASS -- classification: 'transactional' on both sends; blocked-user check in sendLedgeredNotification runs unconditionally before the classification branch and is not bypassed
invariant_verdicts.S11: PASS -- zero log/console/logger calls in any new file; no feedback content or AuditLog payload ever carries it
invariant_verdicts.S13: SIGNED OFF -- migration read directly, purely additive (CREATE TABLE + two nullable ADD COLUMNs), no drop/rename/rewrite of personal-data or attendance-history columns, safe against a live production DB
invariant_verdicts.broadcast_opt_in_consent_boundary: PASS -- writeBroadcastOptInAnswer writes only broadcastOptIn/broadcastOptInAskedAt, never consent_pd_at/consent_pd_version/publish_consent

Read apps/bot/src/domain/feedback.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/feedback.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts, apps/bot/drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql in full
git diff 18f176c a460041 -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts (isolated exactly the feedback table + users.broadcastOptInAskedAt addition, additive only)
Grep for getUserFeedbackStateById/writeBroadcastOptInAnswer/consent_pd/publishConsent in domain/user.ts -- confirmed no shared write path with the three real consent columns
Grep for NotificationKind/blocked/feedback_request/feedback_reminder in domain/notification.ts -- confirmed blocked check unconditional, before classification branch
